items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Then my mother met and married Jimmy Briggs around 1941... He was a great man. He helped to give me a life. I have a great deal of respect for him.

ctx.x: When does Jimmy Briggs come into the picture?

My mother was raising me by myself during all these years. I had one gentleman that was like my godfather, named Norman Cobbs. From the time I was five years old, he was helping my mother raise me, in a sense, taking me to the Y[MCA], taking me – putting me in the Boy Scouts, taking me to church every Sunday, Sunday school, church. Went to Abyssinian Baptist Church, where he played the soprano saxophone in the church ensemble. Then my mother met and married Jimmy Briggs around 1941. We moved from where we lived…
Your godfather, did he give you your first saxophone?
